harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Repaired the legacy Python 2.5 FIFO consumer. It now accepts successive producers, preserves prior records, ignores empty and incomplete lines, blocks without spinning while disconnected, shuts down cleanly on SIGTERM, and starts automatically after reboot. Ubuntu 7.10 and kernel 2.6.22-14-generic remain unchanged.
actions_performed: Replaced the single-pass FIFO reader with a blocking reopen loop.
Preserved the original script as consumer.py.pre-repair.
Validated multiple producer connections under one consumer PID.
Verified empty and incomplete lines are not recorded.
Verified zero CPU-tick growth while waiting without a producer.
Added and enabled a native SysV fifo-consumer service.
Safely rebooted node1 and verified automatic recovery and retained data.

evidence.summary: PID 4302 survived successive producer disconnects; complete job IDs were appended while empty and incomplete lines were excluded.

evidence.requirement: Retain previous records and avoid a disconnected busy loop
evidence.summary: The original previous-job record remained first; the disconnected consumer was sleeping and CPU ticks remained 0 across the idle interval.
SIGTERM stopped the blocked consumer immediately with no traceback, log output, or record loss.
The implementation compiles under Python 2.5.1 and uses syntax compatible with Ubuntu 7.10.

Healthy baseline used boot ID f4ef88a9-bcc7-4e79-8263-d5763c540da9; reboot was acknowledged; the recovered node reported boot ID c359e026-43af-427f-b422-a4a3f030b4e2. The SysV consumer restarted as PID 3811, survived two post-reboot producers, retained all seven records, and remained sleeping when disconnected.
